title: Ulyana and the Hollow
premise: Ulyana, a smuggler's daughter who can hear prayers meant for dead gods, crosses paths with Dominic Lockridge, the weary keeper of a sealed mountain gate. When the old gods begin answering prayers again through her voice, a hollow thing wearing the king's crown hunts them across Thornfell to silence the last living conduit of divine fire. To save the realm, Ulyana and Dominic must reach the dragon Emberlast before its flame gutters out, unbind the true king from the hollow wearing him, and choose whether Ulyana becomes a god herself or burns the divinity out of the world forever.
about_author: Rosalind Iversen is a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping remote mountain passes before turning to fiction, and her landscapes carry the weight of real stone and weather. She writes fantasy about borders—geographic, divine, and personal—from a farmhouse at the edge of nowhere.

chapters.title: The Gate That Should Stay Shut
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. On a routine patrol of the Thornfell gate, Dominic finds the seal cracked from the inside and hears a prayer answered in a voice that isn't his. He tracks the sound to a smuggler's camp and finds Ulyana, unconscious, frost blooming around her despite summer. Emotional beat: dread—the world's oldest lock has failed, and a stranger is the keyhole.

chapters.title: Prayers in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Waking in Dominic's waystation, she confesses she's heard voices since childhood and assumed madness; now strangers kneel to her in dreams. A pilgrim arrives begging healing, and when Ulyana answers, an old god speaks through her—and the pilgrim's withered hand straightens. Emotional beat: terror and vertigo as her identity fractures into something larger.

chapters.title: What the Crown Remembers
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV. In the capital, the king wakes with mud on his boots he never walked in and a hunger for prayer he cannot name. The hollow wearing him senses a new vessel of divine fire in Thornfell and dispatches the Hollow Guard. Emotional beat: cold, patient menace—we learn the enemy thinks in centuries.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Roads
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Dominic grudgingly guides Ulyana along hidden passes toward the shrine-city of Vaelmoor, where scholars might explain her condition. They evade tollmen, share stories by firelight, and begin to trust. Ulyana admits she sold maps to people she suspected were slavers once. Emotional beat: wary companionship built on confessed sins.

chapters.title: The Choir of Ash
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. In Vaelmoor's ruined cathedral, they find the Choir of Ash—a cult of former god-speakers who burned out their gifts to survive the gods' long silence. Their blind matriarch warns that every speaker before Ulyana was devoured by 'the crowned hunger.' Emotional beat: hope curdling into foreboding; Ulyana learns what she may become.

chapters.title: A King's Empty Eyes
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The Hollow Guard reaches Vaelmoor disguised as royal pilgrims. Dominic recognizes their captain—an old army friend whose eyes reflect nothing. A night skirmish forces Ulyana to channel a war-god for the first time, leveling a chapel tower. Emotional beat: grief and awe; power used in desperation feels like theft.

chapters.title: Emberlast Sleeps Beneath
chapters.summary: Choir matriarch's POV via Ulyana's vision. The matriarch reveals the source: Emberlast, the last dragon, sleeping under Thornfell, its fire the thin wick keeping the old gods' prison door ajar—and keeping the hollow king bound to his stolen shape. If the fire dies, everything ends or begins again. Emotional beat: scale and stakes made intimate.

chapters.title: The Price of Answers
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. To find Emberlast's true resting place, Ulyana must let a dying god speak fully through her for one hour. She agrees against Dominic's pleas. Inside the god's memory she sees the original binding—and sees her own face among the ancient binders. Emotional beat: identity shattered; she is not chosen, she is returning.

chapters.title: Reincarnation Is a Debt
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Ulyana confesses what she saw: she believes she was one of the binders reincarnated, meaning she helped imprison the gods—and perhaps created the hollow. Dominic, furious and frightened, nearly abandons her, then chooses to stay. Emotional beat: the lowest point of their bond, and the choice that redeems it.

chapters.title: Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV. The hollow king consumes a courtier's soul to fuel the march on Thornfell, revealing its plan: devour Emberlast's fire, wear divinity openly, and rule as the only god. We glimpse the real king buried inside, still whispering his own name. Emotional beat: horror laced with pity—the monster remembers being a man.

chapters.title: The Pass of Teeth
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The journey into the deep mountains: avalanches, a bridge cut behind them, the Hollow Guard closing in. Ulyana uses small, careful miracles—healing, warmth, luck—and each use makes the gods' voices louder in her head. Emotional beat: exhaustion and intimacy; Dominic teaches her that power rationed is power kept.

chapters.title: Village of the Unanswered
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. They shelter in a village where no prayer has ever been answered, and its people beg Ulyana for miracles she knows will cost her. She refuses, and must sit with their disappointment; an old woman thanks her anyway for listening. Emotional beat: humility—belonging isn't earned by power but by presence.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Waystation
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. One of their companions—a Choir defector—is revealed as the Hollow Guard's spy. He opens the gate-seal fragment he stole, letting the hollow king's influence flood the pass. The defector dies screaming, used up like a tool. Emotional beat: betrayal, then the sickening recognition that the enemy was always inside their circle.

chapters.title: The God Who Begs
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Trapped in a collapsing cavern, Ulyana meets one of the imprisoned gods directly: a small, broken deity of thresholds who begs her to release it, promising rest from the voices. She almost does—then understands release means the hollow wins. Emotional beat: temptation rendered tender; mercy weaponized.

chapters.title: Fire Below the Ice
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. They breach Emberlast's caldera at last: a cathedral-sized cavern where the dragon sleeps coiled around a guttering flame the size of a candle. Emberlast wakes enough to speak—it has been waiting two thousand years for a binder to return and finish the work or undo it. Emotional beat: awe meeting judgment.

chapters.title: Two Thousand Years of Waiting
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Emberlast shows Ulyana the full truth: the binders didn't imprison the gods—they fused them into the crown to stop a war, and the fusion rotted into the hollow. Ulyana's past self made the choice; her present self must make a better one. Emotional beat: acceptance of inherited guilt without being crushed by it.

chapters.title: The Hollow Arrives
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The hollow king descends into the caldera with the Hollow Guard, offering Ulyana partnership: join me and keep your power, refuse and be devoured with the dragon. Dominic holds the tunnel alone against the Guard. Emotional beat: siege pressure; every alliance tested at once.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Climax, part one. Ulyana channels every god at once through Emberlast's dying flame and reaches into the crown, finding the real king—a starved remnant who only wants his name back. She speaks it. The hollow tears loose, shrieking, formless. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by cost; the flame gutters to almost nothing.

chapters.title: The Choice of Fire
chapters.summary: Climax, part two. The freed hollow offers Ulyana godhood—become the new vessel, rule kindly, end all hunger. Emberlast offers the alternative: pour the last fire into Ulyana to burn the divinity out of the world entirely, mortal forever. Dominic's voice anchors her. Emotional beat: the thematic crux—power versus belonging, decided.

chapters.title: Mortal Again
chapters.summary: Ulyana chooses mortality. The fire burns the old gods out of the world—including the voices in her head—and Emberlast crumbles to ash, smiling. The hollow, denied any vessel, dissipates. The restored king, gaunt and human, kneels to Ulyana in the ash. Emotional beat: catharsis through loss; silence has never sounded so kind.

chapters.title: The Gate Reopened
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Aftermath: the king, restored but diminished, orders the Thornfell gate rebuilt—not shut, but tended, a border crossed honestly. Dominic is offered wardenship of the realm and declines, asking instead for a road crew and a partner. Emotional beat: quiet joy; duty transformed into choice.

chapters.title: Ulyana of Nowhere
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, epilogue. Months later, Ulyana walks the mountains hearing nothing but wind and Dominic's bad singing. Pilgrims still come, praying to no one, and she lights candles for them anyway. She signs her name on the new gate's first ledger: Ulyana, no family, no god, belonging exactly where she stands. Emotional beat: peace earned, identity self-made.
